items.question:
Complete the collocation:
Rather than treating the symptoms, the new policy aims to ___ the root causes of homelessness.
items.explanation: We say “address the root causes”. Full sentence: Rather than treating the symptoms, the new policy aims to address the root causes of homelessness.

items.question:
Complete the collocation:

items.explanation: We say “wield power”. Full sentence: A handful of tech companies now wield enormous power over what information we see.

items.question:
Complete the collocation:
Lobby groups ___ considerable pressure on politicians to weaken the regulations.
items.explanation: We say “exert pressure (on)”. Full sentence: Lobby groups exert considerable pressure on politicians to weaken the regulations.

items.question:
Complete the collocation:
Although she accepted the job, she still ___ doubts about whether it was the right move.
items.explanation: We say “harbour doubts”. Full sentence: Although she accepted the job, she still harboured doubts about whether it was the right move.

items.question:
Complete the collocation:
Any customer who cancels less than 24 hours in advance will ___ a cancellation fee.
items.explanation: We say “incur a fee / costs”. Full sentence: Any customer who cancels less than 24 hours in advance will incur a cancellation fee.

items.question:
Complete the collocation:

items.explanation: We say “allay fears”. Full sentence: The airline tried to allay passengers' fears by publishing its safety record.

items.question:

items.explanation: We say “forge a partnership”. Full sentence: The university has forged a partnership with several local hospitals.

items.question:

items.question:
Complete the collocation:

items.explanation: We say “sow the seeds (of)”. Full sentence: Many historians argue that the treaty sowed the seeds of the next war.

items.question:

items.explanation: We say “defy expectations”. Full sentence: The film defied expectations by becoming the most successful release of the year.

items.question:

items.explanation: We say “draw a distinction”. Full sentence: It is important to draw a distinction between criticism of a policy and criticism of a person.

items.question:

items.explanation: We say “meet the criteria”. Full sentence: Unfortunately, your application does not meet the criteria for this scholarship.

items.question:

items.explanation: We say “attach importance (to)”. Full sentence: Employers increasingly attach great importance to communication skills.

items.question:

items.explanation: We say “exercise caution”. Full sentence: Drivers are advised to exercise caution, as many roads are covered in ice.

items.question:

items.question:

At the ceremony, the president ___ tribute to the volunteers who had helped after the floods.
items.explanation: We say “pay tribute (to)”. Full sentence: At the ceremony, the president paid tribute to the volunteers who had helped after the floods.

items.question:
Complete the collocation:
If you are unhappy with the decision, you may ___ a formal complaint with the regulator.
items.explanation: We say “lodge a complaint”. Full sentence: If you are unhappy with the decision, you may lodge a formal complaint with the regulator.

items.question:

items.question:

items.question:

items.question:

items.question:

items.question:

items.question:

items.question:

items.question:

items.explanation: We say “a scathing review”. Full sentence: The critic wrote a scathing review, calling the play 'three hours of my life I'll never get back'.
